topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: Efficiency fluctuations in the 57-66 GHz band stem from array factor and interference. Dynamic beam tiling divides the spectrum into subbands, minimizing overlap and interference. Interfering beams can be mitigated by spreading beams with narrower beams, reducing cross-polarization interference.  Adaptive predistortion compensates for phase noise, enhancing signal quality in noisy environments. These strategies balance bandwidth utilization, signal strength, and interference management to achieve optimal performance while mitigating fluctuations.
reference_context: The 57-66 GHz band experiences significant efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) due to the array factor and interferences. Dynamic beam tiling divides the spectrum into subbands to reduce overlap, reducing interference. Narrow beams minimize cross-polarization interference. Digital predistortion compensates for phase noise, improving signal quality in noisy environments. These techniques balance bandwidth utilization, signal strength, and interference management for optimal performance.
